reads_as: looking out a spacecraft canopy at a blazing alien sunset
layout_map: Full-bleed photographic scene with no big headline. A dark cockpit/canopy frame arcs across the upper-middle (cells 6-7-8, the bright glowing sun-burst gap centered at ~x640,y90 in cell 7) and the curved dashboard/instrument panel fills the bottom center (cells 14-15-16, dark silhouette with small UI controls ~x640,y560). Warm orange-yellow cloudy atmosphere glows behind, brightest at top center, darkening to the edges. Tiny white all-caps subtitle caption sits dead-center bottom in cell 15 (~x640,y585, 'IT TOOK 13 MINUTES...'). No accent-colored headline word; the glow itself is the device.
why_it_works: Puts you inside the spacecraft POV — the immersive first-person frame makes an alien place feel reachable.
mimic_for: an immersive first-person reveal — putting the viewer inside a place or machine they could never actually enter
title: The First Photos On Venus’ Surface

reads_as: a glowing branching ice-continent floating in dark space, like a scan of Antarctica
layout_map: Dead-center hero object on a near-black background. A bright tan/cyan branching landmass (Antarctica-like, veined with magenta-pink coastline) is centered at ~x640,y360 filling cells 6-7-10-11, roughly 40% of the frame, glowing against the black void. Faint dark blue ocean texture in the corners. A tiny dim grey label sits at the very top center (~x640,y20) and a small white all-caps subtitle strip is centered at the bottom in cell 15 (~x640,y585, 'AND THIS ONE IS...'). No big headline; the isolated glowing object on black is the whole composition.
why_it_works: An isolated, glowing, scan-like object on black reads as a precious specimen or scientific find — clean and mysterious.
mimic_for: showcasing a single subject as a specimen — a map, organ, structure, or dataset isolated and glowing on black
title: They Moved the South Pole. And They'll Do It Again.

reads_as: a credit card pulled apart into floating glowing layers, like an x-ray of how it works
layout_map: Exploded-view diagram on a dark blue blueprint-grid background (faint cyan grid lines fill the whole frame). A credit card is split into stacked translucent layers floating diagonally across the center, occupying cells 6-7-10-11 (stack centered ~x650,y230, descending toward lower-right). A red label 'CONTACT PAD' with a thin leader line points to the top layer at ~x430,y55 (cell 2/3), and a yellow up-arrow with 'CHIP' label points up into the card stack from ~x430,y360 (cell 10). Faint ghosted card outlines in the left corners. Small white all-caps subtitle at bottom center cell 15 (~x640,y585, 'HERE'S THE...'). Accent device = the yellow callout arrow plus red leader labels.
why_it_works: The exploded blueprint promises a satisfying 'how it actually works' teardown of an everyday object you've never thought about.
mimic_for: a teardown / how-it-works explainer — pulling a familiar object apart into labeled layers to reveal hidden mechanism
title: What actually happens when I tap a credit card?

reads_as: the Moon locked inside a red targeting reticle, like it's about to be destroyed
layout_map: Dark space background with a faint red HUD grid overlaid across the whole frame. The Moon sits dead-center at ~x640,y360 (cell 11), small-to-mid (~25% of frame), wrapped in concentric red targeting-reticle rings and crosshair brackets centered on it. A small red 'TARGET' label sits just above center at ~x640,y45 (cell 3). A bright red-orange curved arc/explosion sweep crosses the lower third (~y480, cells 13-14-15). Tiny white all-caps subtitle at bottom center cell 15 (~x640,y590, 'OKAY, LET'S BLOW IT UP'). Device = red targeting circle + danger-red palette.
why_it_works: A targeting reticle on something untouchable (the Moon) signals imminent catastrophe — high-stakes hypothetical that demands you watch.
mimic_for: a destructive what-if or threat scenario — locking a target/reticle on something to signal it's about to be destroyed or attacked
title: What If The Moon EXPLODED?

reads_as: staring down a golden symmetrical machine tunnel at a bright collision point
layout_map: One-point-perspective shot looking straight down the throat of a golden/copper-toned industrial machine (particle collider interior). The vanishing point with a bright white-blue glowing flash/collision sits dead-center at ~x640,y360 (cell 11), with the symmetric machine walls receding from all four corners toward it. Warm amber tones dominate the surrounding structure (cells 5-6-7-8-9-10-12). Small white all-caps subtitle at bottom center cell 15 (~x640,y585). No headline text; the glowing center-point + radial symmetry is the whole pull.
why_it_works: Radial one-point perspective forces the eye straight to the glowing collision point — a hypnotic 'into the machine' pull.
mimic_for: going deep inside a machine or system — a symmetric tunnel/vanishing-point shot toward a glowing core or moment of action
title: How Do They Make Particles Hit Each Other?

reads_as: the curved edge of Earth seen from space, a glowing blue arc on black
layout_map: Dark space background, mostly empty/black at the edges (cells 1-5-9-13 and 4-8-12-16 are dark cloudy earth-at-night). The bright blue curved limb of Earth (a horizon arc) sits across the upper-center, cells 6-7 (arc apex ~x640,y110), the glowing atmosphere band catching light. Below it dark land/cloud cover fills the lower-middle. A small white all-caps subtitle is centered at the bottom in cell 15 (~x640,y585, 'WOULD WE NOTICE IF?'). No headline; the single glowing curved horizon on black carries it.
why_it_works: The visible curve of Earth is the silent counter-argument to the flat-earth premise — the image itself is the hook's punchline.
mimic_for: a single striking image that quietly disproves or reframes a premise — let the photo make the argument, no text needed
title: What If The Earth Was Flat?

reads_as: a lone astronaut in a spacesuit standing in space with the Moon beside them
layout_map: Dark starfield background. A spacesuited astronaut (helmet with bright orange/gold reflective visor) stands centered, head-and-shoulders at ~x640,y320 filling cells 7-10-11, the white suit catching warm light. A small grey-white Moon hangs at upper-right ~x880,y110 (cell 8). Faint dim text strip near top center (~x640,y30). Small white all-caps subtitle centered at bottom in cell 15 (~x640,y560, 'FOR THE FIRST TIME...'). The figure is centered rather than offset; no big headline — the suited figure on black is the subject.
why_it_works: A lone human figure in the void makes the achievement personal and aspirational — you project yourself into the suit.
mimic_for: a human-achievement or 'first person to do X' beat — a single suited/equipped figure centered against an awe-scale backdrop
title: New Artemis III Astronauts Just Announced

reads_as: a glittering pink-blue diamond on a stone pedestal surrounded by floating question marks
layout_map: Tall grey stone pedestal/column rises from the bottom center (base fills cells 14-15-16, ~x640,y600). On top of it, dead-center at ~x640,y110 (cell 2/3 boundary, just above mid-top), sits a small bright sparkling crystal/diamond in pink-cyan iridescent tones. Several chunky 3D question marks float around it in green, yellow, magenta and cyan — at ~x510,y55, ~x720,y45, ~x800,y110, ~x550,y170, and a large yellow one lower-right ~x950,y370 (cell 12). Dark blue-grey gradient background with faint grid. Small white all-caps subtitle centered at bottom cell 15 (~x640,y560, 'DIAMONDS ACTUALLY ARE...'). Device = the glowing gem + colorful question-mark cluster signaling mystery.
why_it_works: The prized object on a pedestal ringed by question marks frames it as a riddle — 'there's a secret about this thing you don't know.'
mimic_for: a mystery/curiosity-gap beat about one prized object — pedestal it and surround with question marks to say 'the truth will surprise you'
title: How Old Diamonds REALLY Are
